question: Does the 2019 Makati Public Rail EIS provide fish records from its Pasig River stations, or only a historical reported-species list?
citation: Philippine Infradev Holdings, Inc. (2019). Environmental Impact Statement: Makati Public Rail Transport System Project. Prepared by Lichel Technologies, Inc. Official copy hosted by the DENR Environmental Management Bureau EIA portal.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the official EMB-hosted PDF text view on 2026-11-19; no PDF or page image was retained.
sourceLocators: Freshwater Ecology, Table 2-29 and report pages 2-91 to 2-92: five named Pasig stations with coordinates; plankton and benthos procedures.

Page 2-92: the EIS explicitly states fish sampling was not successfully done because the available barge was unsuitable for electrofishing and intermittent rain prevented use of the gear along steep cemented banks.
Table 2-31, report pages 2-94: a separate ‘Reported Species in Pasig River’ list with remarks; it is not a fish capture matrix for the five stations.

samplingReview.coordinateUseDecision: These are source-reported freshwater-ecology station points for plankton and benthos sampling. They are not fish-capture coordinates and are retained here only to prevent future misattribution; no points or geometry are added to Bangwit.
samplingReview.fishMethodAsReported: Electrofishing was intended, but the report says fish sampling was unsuccessful because the MMDA barge was unsuitable for the gear and intermittent rains prevented using it along steep cemented banks.
samplingReview.fishSurveyOutcome: No successful fish collection or station-resolved fish dataset is reported for these five stations.
otherBiotaMethods: Phytoplankton and zooplankton were sampled with an 80 micrometre plankton net.
One Ekman grab sample was collected per station for benthos.
samplingReview.dateLimitation: No fish-specific collection date is available because fish sampling was unsuccessful. The reviewed station table does not attach a fish observation date to the reported-species list.

reportedFishList.interpretation: A historical, mixed-provenance source summary, distinct from the unsuccessful station fish survey. The source does not provide a reconciled species-by-station matrix, fish vouchers, specimen catalog numbers, or a complete occurrence provenance for every row.

entriesAsPrinted.sourceRemark: Described as common and pollution tolerant; the EIS says it is unsure whether the fish could breed within the Pasig stretch.
entriesAsPrinted.provenanceClass: reported summary; row cites no underlying survey or specimen
entriesAsPrinted.decision: Research-only; no current occurrence or residency assertion.

entriesAsPrinted.provenanceClass: reported summary; shared remark also spans the following row
entriesAsPrinted.decision: Preserve source spelling; taxon and locality are not independently validated.

reportedFishList.taxonomyDecision: The EIS's spelling ‘Pterygoplychthys’ is preserved verbatim. No independent taxonomic resolution is made in this review.

rightsAndEvidenceDecision.decision: Keep as an attributed, research-only source review. Public hosting does not establish permission to republish its table, maps, photographs, or derived species records.

limits: This EIS is a project report, not a systematic or current Pasig River fish inventory.
The five station coordinates belong to non-fish ecology sampling; fish sampling was unsuccessful.
The separate reported-fish list mixes an informal observation, secondary citations, washout context, and entries without item-level provenance.
No listed name establishes present-day occurrence, abundance, residency, fishability, legal access, safety, or diet/bait advice.
nextActions: Keep all eight source-listed names out of public species and occurrence projections until their cited evidence is independently retrieved and reviewed.
Trace Orozco & Zafaralla (2012) and identify whether it gives direct Pasig localities, dates, methods, and reusable data.
Continue the NCR freshwater, brackish, tidal, and marine search across the incomplete waterbody scope.
